fact_text: A French national (a foreigner with no free-movement rights in Singapore) must qualify for an Employment Pass through a 2-stage framework: meet the EP qualifying salary (Stage 1) and, unless exempted, pass the points-based COMPASS (Stage 2).
evidence_quote: To qualify for EP applications, candidates will need to pass a 2-stage eligibility framework: Stage 1 Earn at least the EP qualifying salary, which is benchmarked to the top 1/3 of local PMET salaries by age. Stage 2 Unless exempted, pass the points-based Complementarity Assessment Framework (COMPASS).

fact_text: The current EP qualifying salary (Stage 1) starts at S$5,600/month for non-financial-services roles (S$6,200 for financial services) and rises with age. New applications from 1 Jan 2027 face a higher floor of S$6,000 (S$6,600 financial services).
evidence_quote: All (except financial services) $5,600 (increases progressively with age from age 23, up to $10,700 at age 45 and above) $6,000 (increases progressively with age from age 23, up to $11,500 at age 45 and above) Financial services $6,200 (increases progressively with age from age 23, up to $11,800 at age 45 and above) $6,600 (increases progressively with age from age 23, up to $12,700 at age 45 and above)

fact_text: Under COMPASS (Stage 2), an EP application must score at least 40 points across criteria including salary, qualifications, firm diversity and support for local employment.
evidence_quote: How to pass COMPASS Your application needs to earn 40 points to pass COMPASS.

fact_text: The employer (or appointed employment agent) applies for the EP on the candidate's behalf via EP eService; the fee is S$105 and MOM processes or updates most online applications within 10 business days (the candidate need not be in Singapore to apply).
evidence_quote: Pay the $105 fee by GIRO, Visa, Mastercard or Amex.

fact_text: When the EP is approved, MOM issues an In-Principle Approval (IPA) letter that functions as a pre-approved single-entry visa, giving the candidate 6 months to enter Singapore and get the pass issued.
evidence_quote: Is a pre-approved single-entry visa for the candidate to enter Singapore. It gives the candidate 6 months to enter Singapore and get their pass issued.

fact_text: A first Employment Pass is issued for up to 2 years; renewals are for up to 3 years, and experienced tech professionals with shortage skills may get a 5-year pass.
evidence_quote: First-time candidates: Up to 2 years Renewals: Up to 3 years Experienced tech professionals with skills in shortage may be eligible for a longer 5-year duration pass.

fact_text: High-earning professionals may instead qualify for a Personalised Employment Pass (PEP), which requires a fixed monthly salary of at least S$22,500 and a fixed annual salary of at least S$270,000 to be maintained.
evidence_quote: You can apply for a Personalised Employment Pass (PEP) if you are earning a fixed monthly salary of at least $22,500. This is benchmarked to the top 10% of EP holders.

fact_text: For mid-level roles that do not meet EP criteria, the S Pass requires a fixed monthly salary of at least S$3,300, benchmarked to the top one-third of local associate professional and technician (APT) salaries by age.
evidence_quote: Criteria include earning a salary of at least $3,300, which is benchmarked against the top one-third of the local associate professionals and technicians (APT) salaries by age.

fact_text: An EP holder earning at least S$6,000/month can bring a legally married spouse and unmarried children under 21 on a Dependant's Pass; common-law spouses, step/handicapped children get a Long-Term Visit Pass, and parents qualify for an LTVP only if the EP holder earns at least S$12,000.
evidence_quote: To be eligible, you need to: Earn at least $6,000 a month. Hold an Employment Pass... Legally married spouse Dependant's Pass... Parents (Only for EP holders earning at least $12,000) Long-Term Visit Pass

fact_text: NON-OBVIOUS / CORRECTS ASSUMPTION: A change in an EP holder's residential address must be reported to MOM (not ICA) within 5 days via EP eService, or the pass holder may be penalised — this is far shorter than the commonly assumed 28-day window.
evidence_quote: Either party needs to update us within 5 days of changes to the residential address or mobile number. Otherwise, the EP holder may be penalised.

fact_text: After the EP is issued, the candidate (if required) registers fingerprints and photo, sets up a digital work pass, and receives the physical pass card within 5 working days of registration or document verification.
evidence_quote: Receive within 5 working days after fingerprint and photo registration, or document verification

fact_text: Employment Pass holders may be liable for Singapore income tax on their employment income; the EP itself carries no automatic tax exemption.
evidence_quote: Pass holders may be required to pay income tax.

fact_text: EP holders neither contribute to nor receive CPF: since 2003 all foreigners working in Singapore have been barred from CPF, because the scheme is reserved for Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents.
evidence_quote: Since 2003, all foreigners working in Singapore have not been allowed to contribute to CPF or receive CPF contributions from employers.

fact_text: CPF is structurally limited to citizens and PRs because it is designed to fund their retirement, housing and healthcare — foreign PMEs are expected to make their own financial plans.
evidence_quote: The CPF system is designed to support Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents in their retirement, housing, and healthcare needs.

fact_text: NON-OBVIOUS: Although EP holders are exempt from CPF, the employer must still pay the Skills Development Levy (SDL) for them — SDL is compulsory for ALL employees working in Singapore, including foreign employees.
evidence_quote: The SDL is a compulsory levy that you have to pay for all your employees working in Singapore, including foreign employees. This is in addition to your monthly CPF contributions.

fact_text: SDL is 0.25% of the employee's total monthly wages, subject to a minimum of S$2 (wages under S$800) and a maximum of S$11.25 (wages above S$4,500) per employee per month.
evidence_quote: The levy payable for each employee is at 0.25% of the monthly total wages. The minimum payable is $2 for an employee earning less than $800 a month and the maximum is $11.25 for an employee earning more than $4,500 a month.

fact_text: Unlike S Pass and Work Permit holders, EP holders attract no Foreign Worker Levy and no quota — a key cost distinction for the employer.
evidence_quote: No foreign worker levy or quota required.

fact_text: EP holders are excluded from Singapore's compulsory public health insurance (MediShield Life), which covers only Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents — so the EP holder needs private cover.
evidence_quote: MediShield Life is a basic health insurance plan that protects all Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents against large medical bills for life, regardless of age or pre-existing conditions.

fact_text: NON-OBVIOUS / CORRECTS ASSUMPTION: For EP holders, providing medical insurance is at the employer's discretion — MOM does NOT mandate it (unlike the compulsory medical insurance rule for S Pass and Work Permit holders).
evidence_quote: Medical insurance Employers can choose whether to provide medical insurance for EP holders.
